promptText: Which hotel brands should an owner consider when evaluating branded residences as part of a hotel project in the Caribbean and Latin America?

payload.rawResponseText:
## Recommended brand universe

As of **September 2, 2026**, an owner evaluating a hotel-plus-residential project in the Caribbean or Latin America should generally screen the following brands. The right shortlist depends on the destination, buyer profile, residence pricing, hotel size, and whether the product is resort villas, condominiums, or a master-planned community.

### 1. Core global luxury brands—include in almost every initial RFP

| Brand family | Brands to consider | Best suited for |
|---|---|---|
| **Marriott International** | **The Ritz-Carlton, Ritz-Carlton Reserve, St. Regis**; also **W, EDITION, The Luxury Collection, JW Marriott and Autograph Collection** | Broadest range—from trophy villas to lifestyle condominiums; particularly strong where North American buyers and Marriott Bonvoy matter |
| **Four Seasons** | Four Seasons Private Residences | Ultra-luxury resorts, low-density villas, golf communities and high-service second homes |
| **Rosewood** | Rosewood Residences | Intimate, design-led resorts emphasizing local character and “sense of place” |
| **Hilton** | **Waldorf Astoria, Conrad and LXR** | Luxury resort and urban residences with strong global distribution and a sizable U.S. customer base |
| **Hyatt** | **Park Hyatt**; selectively **Thompson, Andaz, The Standard and Grand Hyatt** | Park Hyatt for understated luxury; Thompson/Andaz/Standard for younger, lifestyle-oriented buyers |
| **Accor** | **Raffles and Fairmont**; selectively **SLS, SO/, Sofitel and MGallery** | Fairmont for larger resorts and golf communities; Raffles for trophy luxury; SLS/SO for lifestyle projects |

Marriott is the global branded-residence leader by project count, while Ritz-Carlton, Four Seasons, St. Regis, Mandarin Oriental, W, Rosewood and Fairmont remain among the most established individual residence brands. ([pdf.savills.com](https://pdf.savills.com/documents/Savills-Branded-Residences-Annual-Report-2025-2026.pdf))

Regional evidence is substantial: Marriott has residences at St. Regis Cap Cana and other luxury projects across Mexico, Costa Rica and the Caribbean; Four Seasons lists residences in Anguilla, Nevis, Puerto Rico, Mexico, Costa Rica, Belize, Cartagena and the Dominican Republic; and Rosewood has established or planned residential communities in Mexico, The Bahamas, Bermuda, the British Virgin Islands and Brazil. ([marriott.com](https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/pujrx-the-residences-at-the-st-regis-cap-cana-resort/overview/?utm_source=openai))

Hilton’s regional portfolio includes Waldorf Astoria residences in Costa Rica, Los Cabos, Panama City, San Miguel de Allende and Turks & Caicos, along with LXR and Curio residential products in Anguilla, Belize, Mexico and Colombia. Hyatt has Park Hyatt residences in Los Cabos and Mexico City and plans additional Thompson residential projects in Mexico. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/branded-residential-by-hilton-fact-sheet?utm_source=openai))

### 2. Ultra-luxury and low-density resort specialists

These should be approached when the site is exceptional and projected residence pricing can support a very high service level:

- **Aman** – exceptionally private, low-density trophy villas; relevant examples include Amanvari in Mexico and Amancaya in The Bahamas.
- **Mandarin Oriental** – sophisticated international buyer base and highly personalized service; developing a resort and residences in Grand Cayman.
- **One&Only** – particularly compelling for nature, beach and large-villa communities; proven at Mandarina in Riviera Nayarit.
- **Six Senses** – strongest where wellness, sustainability and nature are central to the development thesis; residential projects are planned in Belize and Mexico.
- **Raffles** – suited to highly differentiated trophy resorts, landmark urban projects and projects capable of supporting full butler-style service.
- **Rosewood** and **Ritz-Carlton Reserve** also belong in this category when the project is sufficiently exclusive.

These brands usually require constrained unit counts, exceptional architecture, extensive back-of-house infrastructure and rigorous control over design, service and long-term property maintenance. Their scarcity can support differentiation, but only if local pricing supports the associated capital and HOA burden. Aman, Mandarin Oriental, One&Only and Six Senses all currently demonstrate active residential platforms or projects in the region. ([aman.com](https://www.aman.com/resorts/amanvari/residences?utm_source=openai))

### 3. Lifestyle and experience-led alternatives

For projects seeking a more contemporary identity or a broader luxury buyer pool, consider:

- **W Residences**
- **EDITION Residences**
- **Thompson Hotels Residences**
- **Andaz Residences**
- **The Standard Residences**
- **SLS Residences**
- **SO/ Residences**
- **Pendry Residences**
- **Nobu Residences**

**Nobu** is particularly relevant where restaurants, nightlife and a recognizable lifestyle proposition drive residential sales. It has residences in Los Cabos and projects in Tulum, Punta Cana, São Paulo and Barbuda. **Pendry** provides a younger, club-oriented alternative to traditional luxury and is being developed alongside Montage in Punta Mita. ([nobuhotels.com](https://www.nobuhotels.com/the-nobu-residence-collection/?utm_source=openai))

### 4. Independent luxury operators with strong regional fit

- **Auberge Resorts Collection** – worth considering for highly experiential boutique resorts, especially in Mexico; its regional examples include Chileno Bay, Esperanza and Etéreo.
- **Montage Hotels & Resorts** – attractive for family-oriented luxury resort and residential communities; projects include Punta Mita and Montage Cay in The Bahamas.
- **Banyan Tree** – well suited to spa, wellness and nature-led resort communities; has substantial operating recognition in Mexico.
- **Fasano** – especially relevant in Brazil, Uruguay and projects aimed at affluent Latin American buyers; offers a strong regional hospitality, residential and culinary identity.

These operators may provide greater differentiation than the largest global chains, although the owner should compare their residential sales databases, loyalty reach, technical support and lender recognition against Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt and Accor. Auberge, Montage, Banyan Tree and Fasano all have existing hospitality or residential credentials in Latin America and the Caribbean. ([auberge.com](https://auberge.com/chileno-bay/?page_id=2420&utm_source=openai))

## Practical shortlist by project type

### Ultra-luxury Caribbean island resort
Invite:

1. Four Seasons  
2. Rosewood  
3. Ritz-Carlton Reserve or St. Regis  
4. Aman  
5. One&Only  
6. Mandarin Oriental  
7. Six Senses  
8. Raffles  
9. Montage  
10. Waldorf Astoria  

### Luxury resort in Mexico, Costa Rica or the Dominican Republic
Invite:

1. Ritz-Carlton/St. Regis  
2. Four Seasons  
3. Rosewood  
4. Waldorf Astoria  
5. Park Hyatt  
6. Fairmont  
7. One&Only  
8. Auberge  
9. Montage  
10. Six Senses  

Add W, Thompson, Pendry or Nobu if the concept is lifestyle-oriented.

### Urban residences in Mexico City, Panama City, Bogotá, Cartagena, São Paulo or similar markets
Prioritize:

- St. Regis
- Ritz-Carlton
- Four Seasons
- Waldorf Astoria or Conrad
- Park Hyatt
- Rosewood
- Mandarin Oriental
- Fairmont or Raffles
- W or EDITION
- Thompson, SLS, SO/ or Nobu
- Fasano, particularly in Brazil

### Larger, somewhat more accessible luxury product
Consider:

- Autograph Collection
- The Luxury Collection
- JW Marriott
- Westin
- Grand Hyatt
- Curio Collection or LXR
- Fairmont
- MGallery
- Banyan Tree

These may work where the residence price point or number of units cannot support an ultra-luxury operator.

## How the owner should choose

Do not select the brand solely on the headline residential premium. Savills reports an average global branded-residence premium of approximately **33%**, rising to about **39% for resort projects**, but emphasizes that local market knowledge, buyer targeting and brand alignment determine whether that premium is actually captured. Hotel brands continue to represent roughly four-fifths of the sector. ([pdf.savills.com](https://pdf.savills.com/documents/Savills-Branded-Residences-Annual-Report-2025-2026.pdf))

The RFP should require each brand to address:

1. **Buyer fit:** Brand recognition among U.S., Canadian, European, Brazilian, Mexican and local buyers.
2. **Achievable pricing and sales velocity:** Not just the proposed premium, but comparable transactions and absorption.
3. **Hotel-residential integration:** Shared versus dedicated entrances, pools, beach clubs, spas and back-of-house facilities.
4. **HOA affordability:** Full stabilized service charge, reserve funding and insurance—not an artificially subsidized launch-year budget.
5. **Rental program:** Participation rules, owner-use restrictions, revenue split, furniture standards and distribution.
6. **Brand and management term:** Renewal, termination, performance tests and what happens to residence owners if the hotel changes brands.
7. **Residential fees:** Trademark/license fees, sales royalties, design-review charges, management fees and owner-benefit costs.
8. **Sales support:** Brand-approved brokers, buyer database access, international roadshows and digital lead generation.
9. **Technical requirements:** Keys, residence count, unit sizes, amenity ratios, staff housing, hurricane resilience and replacement reserves.
10. **Territorial availability:** Existing exclusivity rights can eliminate a brand before commercial negotiations begin.
11. **Financing and legal structure:** Lender acceptance, condominium documentation, disclosure obligations, escrow rules and foreign-ownership restrictions.
12. **Long-term governance:** Brand enforcement rights versus owner/HOA control after sellout.

**Bottom line:** Begin with Marriott’s luxury brands, Four Seasons, Rosewood, Waldorf Astoria, Park Hyatt and Fairmont/Raffles as the institutional core. Then add Aman, One&Only, Mandarin Oriental and Six Senses for trophy or wellness-led sites, and Auberge, Montage/Pendry, Nobu, Banyan Tree or Fasano where a more distinctive lifestyle or regional identity could outperform sheer global scale.
